newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Petroz says Timor Gap well suspended.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Petroz says Timor Gap well suspended.

text.p: Oil and gas producer Petroz NL said on Wednesday the Kakatua North-1A exploration well in the Timor Gap off the coast of northwestern Australia has been suspended as a future oil producer.
Petroz reported last week that the well in Block 91-12 of the Timor Sea Zone of Cooperation (ZOCA) with Indonesia had encountered a gross hydrocarbon column of about 70 metres.
An oil sample measuring 55.6 API gravity was obtained by wireline from a depth of 3,158.5 metres.
Petroz said the well was expected to have a positive impact on the development of the Elang and Kakatua oilfieds, 525km northwest of Darwin.
The development of the oil fields was officially approved last week by the Australia-Indonesia Timor Gap Joint Authority.
Operator Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said the project was expected to cost A$94 million, and oil production was due to begin in the third quarter of 1998.
BHP holds 42.417 percent of ZOCA 91-12, Santos Ltd 21.426 percent, Indonesia's Inpex Sahul Ltd 21.209 percent, and Petroz 14.948 percent.
